item.title: What kind of questions can we ask the I Ching?
item.description:
Quite recently, I saw a post on reddit with a very important question. So much so that I decided to write an article about it with my answer. Here is the original question:

What questions the i ching do not answer ?
#

I am not asking “what is best to ask” (example “ask on how to be a better person”) Also i am not asking “how to phrase the questions so i can get the clearest answer” So not the usual yes/no questions debate (though if someone wants to add about this stuff above , than it is an appreciated bonus , but just as an added thing about the topic , so a good answer can be : " i ching does not answer questions about what is the tastiest food you can get today , and also you should ask i ching for advice and not “yes/no” questions if you want to get a clear answer" )

item.title: How to Use the Liu Yao Method to Find Lost Objects
item.description: Losing objects is one of the most common situations in daily life. It is also deeply stressful becuase it makes us waste time almost always when we least can afford to. While we could certainly perform a classic I Ching consultation to help us find lost objects, and such consultations can give us clues based on the images in the hexagram texts, consulting the I Ching in the classic way is not the most efficient method for finding lost objects. Did you know that there is a divination method based on the I Ching specifically designed for this kind of situation?

item.title: How to Consult the I Ching Using the Coin Toss Method
item.description: A practical guide to consulting the I Ching by tossing three coins. It explains the numerical value of each throw, how the 6 hexagram lines are built, the difference between fixed and moving lines, and how to identify the resulting and derived hexagrams.

item.title: The ABC of the I Ching
item.description: The I Ching is more than an oracle: it’s a universal language based on Yin and Yang. This article guides you through its binary alphabet, the 8 trigrams, and the 64 hexagrams, explaining how its words and sentences are structured.
